foot_before_hand.diagnosis: The front foot is moving before the weapon arm starts the attack.
foot_before_hand.practice: Practice slow step-lunge reps where the hand clearly leads the foot.

lunge_overextension.diagnosis: The front knee angle suggests the lunge is collapsing past a strong support position.
lunge_overextension.practice: Pause at the end of each lunge and check knee-over-ankle control.

incomplete_arm_extension.diagnosis: The attacking arm is not reaching a clear extension during the lunge.
incomplete_arm_extension.practice: Use extension-lunge drills with a target and freeze the finish.

guard_dropped.diagnosis: The front wrist is dropping below the shoulder line for too long.
guard_dropped.practice: Shadow footwork while keeping the bell/hand in the same visual lane.

stance_too_high.diagnosis: The front knee is too straight for a stable en-garde position.
stance_too_high.practice: Hold en-garde for short intervals and reset when the knees straighten.

bounce_excessive.diagnosis: The pelvis is moving up and down more than needed during footwork.
bounce_excessive.practice: Practice advance-retreat with a quiet head and steady hip height.

center_of_mass_in_front.diagnosis: The body center is drifting too close to the front foot.
center_of_mass_in_front.practice: Reset to balanced en-garde after each step.

center_of_mass_leaning_backward.diagnosis: The body center is drifting too close to the back foot.
center_of_mass_leaning_backward.practice: Use mirror footwork and keep the hips centered between the feet.

over_parrying.diagnosis: The front wrist is traveling wider than needed for a compact defensive action.
over_parrying.practice: Practice small parry-recover reps without letting the hand drift.

wide_step.diagnosis: The foot distance is wider than the shoulder-width reference.
wide_step.practice: Mark a comfortable step length and keep repeated steps inside it.

narrow_step.diagnosis: The foot distance is too narrow for stable fencing footwork.
narrow_step.practice: Reset the feet to a shoulder-aware guard before moving again.
